entries.subject: Tempel 1 Deep Impact normalization using Li 2013 Hapke parameters
entries.finding: The diagnostic trial reduces accepted photographed area from 32.58% to 24.48%; only 11 of 28 common-point overlap pairs improve. Retain the Deep Impact photographs. The original H-function approximation and final fitting phase range remain unverified; the tabulated 550 nm model is applied to a clear filter.
entries.revisitWhen: A verified formulation and matching filter calibration improve both retained terrain coverage and independent overlaps.

entries.subject: Tempel 1 NExT normalization using Li 2013 Hapke parameters
entries.finding: The diagnostic trial reduces accepted photographed area from 56.43% to 34.28%; only 4 of 15 common-point overlap pairs improve. Retain the NExT photographs. The original H-function approximation and final fitting phase range remain unverified; the tabulated 550 nm model is applied to a clear filter.
entries.revisitWhen: A verified formulation and matching filter calibration improve both retained terrain coverage and independent overlaps.

entries.subject: ITS 9000678 intermediate approach frame
entries.finding: The retained survey identifies this 7.026 m/pixel frame between selected wider and finer footprints. It was not selected for the existing composite; no failed per-frame camera fit is recorded.
entries.revisitWhen: A registered footprint demonstrates useful coverage or detail beyond the selected approach sequence.

entries.subject: ITS 9000692 final 64 by 64 window
entries.finding: The retained survey identifies 9000692 among four final windows spanning 2.094 to 0.488 m/pixel. Its small footprint has not been qualified on the current fixed atlas; nominal sampling alone does not establish useful displayed detail.
entries.revisitWhen: The frame passes independent terrain-overlap registration and contributes useful detail at the supported atlas resolution.

entries.subject: PDS v2 Tempel 1 shape and source constraints
entries.finding: The 16,022-vertex, 32,040-triangle source supplies the shape and its stereo, limb and weak-region flags. The shape and constraint views distinguish those methods; weak regions are not claimed as measured terrain.

entries.subject: Eight pre-impact ITS photographs
entries.finding: Frames 9000632, 9000639, 9000644, 9000654, 9000673, 9000675, 9000680 and 9000688 form the existing 2005 mosaic. The three cropped close-ups use relative terrain-overlap registration; they improve detail inside an existing footprint and do not establish metre-accurate absolute terrain.

entries.subject: Six Stardust-NExT NAVCAM photographs
entries.finding: N30033, N30036, N30039, N30042, N30045 and N30048 form the separate 2011 mosaic. The two encounters retain their own photographs and lighting; they are not combined into a surface-change map.

entries.subject: MRI 9000909
entries.finding: The evaluated frame is much coarser, about 88 m per pixel, than the selected ITS approach sequence. It was not selected for the current surface mosaic.
entries.revisitWhen: A registered footprint supplies useful terrain missing from the finer selected sources.

entries.subject: Later 2005 MRI frames
entries.finding: Later frames can include the impact plume; the source note distinguishes spacecraft impact time from Earth reception time. No plume-free registered surface contribution was qualified for these candidates.
entries.revisitWhen: A specific frame has a supported nucleus-only footprint and independently checked camera registration.

entries.subject: 2005 HRI imagery and later SPC shape
entries.finding: Both routes were surveyed without replacing the qualified 2012 source shape. The retained note does not establish a restored matching image, camera and SPC model bundle.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image, camera and matching SPC mesh can be restored together and independently registered.

entries.subject: SBMT source cameras for Tempel 1
entries.finding: The earlier survey lacked access to its SBMT camera files. Shared observation tooling has since changed, but this ledger migration does not establish current access or a matching Tempel source bundle.
entries.revisitWhen: A public or already-authorized Tempel image, pointing and exact model bundle is available for qualification.

entries.subject: Earlier coarse-mesh photometric correction
entries.finding: The original photographic selection retained acquisition shading after coarse-mesh normalization introduced facet patterns. Today's Li-parameter trials are separate entries with measured coverage losses.
entries.revisitWhen: Verified model normals and photometry improve independent overlaps while preserving useful source coverage.

entries.subject: HRI-IR V3 fitted color temperature
entries.finding: The selected 40-exposure scan supplies a fitted temperature field on 1,590 accepted source facets. It is a new fit to calibrated spectra with coarse approximate placement, not a reproduction of the published 2013 temperature map or its uncertainty.

entries.subject: HRI-IR V3 reflected continuum slope
entries.finding: The same accepted scan supplies the 1.5–2.2 micrometre continuum slope after thermal separation. It measures spectral reflectance slope, not terrain steepness or identified minerals; missing spectra remain grid.

entries.subject: Other inbound and outbound HRI-IR scans
entries.finding: Additional scans remain source candidates. The selected scan's alignment and detector checks do not establish their registration or remove their possible coma contributions.
entries.revisitWhen: A specific scan adds useful source facets and passes independent scan-to-shape alignment and spectral-quality checks.

entries.subject: Deep Impact site and smooth regions S1–S4
entries.finding: The site uses the released PDS frame; S1–S4 use representative interiors in Thomas 2013 Fig. 2b. Coordinates are approximate, and the weak shape cells under S1 and S2 do not become precise surveys through label placement.

entries.subject: Reproducing the first cropped ITS camera on current main
entries.finding: During this work, preparation of 9000675 fails the source-scale registration budget with both the unchanged main matcher and the unit-corrected matcher. Their regenerated control records are identical before the gate. Existing shipped photographs remain unchanged; earlier recorded reproduction passes do not establish a current pass.
entries.revisitWhen: The replay discrepancy is traced to its source, camera or software input and both partitions meet the existing budget.
